tonight.headline: Wilson still not cleared — and their Walker is out
body: Bad news first: Garrett Wilson has still not been officially cleared from the concussion protocol. The latest is an expectation, not a ruling — he is 'expected to be cleared' (Matt Zenitz via RotoWire, 14 Nov) and stays questionable. His first cover, Denzel Boston, is a game-day decision on the toe that put him in a walking boot Friday (Footballguys gameday expectations, 14 Nov: 'comes down to how the player feels in pre-game warmups'). Diggs' 20.3 on your bench is the bar that slot has to beat.

Good news after it: the Chiefs ruled Kenneth Walker out on Saturday (groin; Yahoo 14 Nov), and he and Carnell Tate (out, shoulder) are both still in Nicky Jam's starting lineup at 0.0. ESPN now has it 148.1 to 92.3, 80%. The lineup as set is the projection lineup — nothing to tap today. One check, Sunday 10:30 CDMX: Wilson, then Boston.

case.label: Their side
case.body: Walker was downgraded from questionable to out Saturday (Yahoo 14 Nov; ESPN now shows OUT), after the morning brief. Nicky Jam can still fill both dead slots from the bench — Blake Corum (11.6), Jalen Coker (11.3), A.J. Brown (12.6, questionable, ankle/knee) — which would take their projection to roughly 115, still well short of yours. Their last lineup move was Thursday.

case.label: Your check
case.body: If Wilson is inactive at 10:30: Boston if Boston is active, otherwise DK Metcalf, who kicks off at 19:20 and is still movable after the noon games lock. Jets and Browns inactives both land at 10:30.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nicky Jam replacing both zeros and Bijan Robinson (18.7) having a big day — the margin is about 33 projected points after the swaps, so it takes a bust on your side too. Wilson ruled out before kickoff — then the check is a straight swap.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · check Sun 15 Nov 10:30 CDMX
doFirst.title: If Wilson is inactive, start Boston — or Metcalf
doFirst.subtitle: Wilson starts. This is the plan if the protocol's last step fails — Boston is a game-day decision, so Metcalf may be the one.

case.label: The check
case.body: Full practice Friday; still questionable. Saturday's only reporting is an expectation: 'expected to be cleared' (Zenitz via RotoWire 14 Nov), 'Projecting Active' (Footballguys 14 Nov). No official clearance found by 22:00Z. Concussion clearance needs an independent neurologist, so the answer may not come until inactives.

case.label: The cover
case.body: Boston (12.8, toe) missed Wednesday and Thursday, was limited Friday and left in a walking boot. Footballguys lists him a game-day decision (14 Nov). ESPN's 12.8 has not moved, so the boot is still not priced. If he is inactive too, Metcalf (10.6) plays Sunday night at Cincinnati and can still be moved in after noon.

case.label: Who is throwing
case.body: Boston: Deshaun Watson, named the starter over Shedeur Sanders (clevelandbrowns.com). Metcalf: Aaron Rodgers; Derrick Harmon is the only Steeler with a status (steelers.com Friday report).

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Wilson is inactive and the cover scores under Diggs' 20.3 — the Tuesday swap then closes WRONG on its outcome, whatever this card does. The card itself is wrong only if Metcalf outscores Boston after Boston was chosen.

whatWentWrong.title: Diggs scored 20.3 on the bench
whatWentWrong.lead: The Tuesday swap put Wilson in on a 2.0 projection edge. Diggs then drew 10 targets and scored the winner.

case.label: What happened
case.body: Wilson 12.8 against Diggs 10.8 on Tuesday — exactly 2.0, labelled PROJECTION. Diggs: 10 targets, 6 catches, 20.3 (archive), the late touchdown in a 24-21 win (VAVEL 12 Nov).

case.label: Why it was still the call
case.body: Diggs played Thursday, so the slot had to be set before Wilson's status was known. The projection lineup is the policy; the backtest found nothing that beats it.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Wilson (or his cover) scores 20.3 or more — then the swap closes RIGHT. Below it, WRONG on the outcome. Either way it is one decision, not a pattern.

waiverAnalysis.summary: Nine weeks of data. The tool prints the same four receivers as this morning against Diggs, your weakest movable receiver (10.7 a game); nothing at running back or tight end. Role reasons carried from this week's research and re-checked where news moved: none beats this roster this week.
